findings.evidence: "A refusal stops the command. Steps it finished before the refusal (a catch-up push, a fold, earlier merges) stay done, and the report lists them." This is followed by several command bullets that repeat argparse help text (for example `fold.py show <selector>`: read-only. Prints the unit's `state:` and `pr:`.)
findings.fix: Keep the non-obvious behaviour (exit codes, reuse rules, refusals) inline. For the purely descriptive one-liners that `fold.py <cmd> --help` already prints, point to `--help`, or move them to references/unit-contract.md with a record row. Keep any line that changes what the agent does.

findings.evidence: The Unit flow section lists commands and refusals, but nothing says in what order a unit moves through start → boundary → checkpoint → ready → merge-chain. The order is only implied across the GSD hooks and GSD install sections.
findings.fix: Add a short lifecycle checklist at the top of Unit flow: 1) start (runs boundary start), 2) boundary --point plan before planning, 3) guard + boundary --point wave before execution, 4) checkpoint after each wave (--final at the end), 5) ready after verification passes, 6) merge-chain only when the owner asks. Name the refusal to check at each step.

findings.evidence: "- Never fold the base branch or a branch whose PR has merged." / "- Never push without push consent." / "- Never remove the `Ai-Kit-Fold:` trailer from a folded commit." Only the first NEVER item gives a reason.
findings.fix: Give each NEVER item its non-obvious reason. Examples: the Ai-Kit-Fold trailer is what `fold.py status` uses to tell folded plans from unfolded ones, so removing it makes the plan look unfolded and invites a second fold. A merged branch's history is already in the trunk, so rewriting it duplicates commits. Also add a short Gotchas list for environment facts that are currently buried in prose: a bare relative path to gsd-tools capability install is read as a registry name; `config-get --raw` prints a one-entry list as a bare string; the boundary edits `.graphifyignore`, and leaving that change uncommitted makes the checkpoint refuse with dirty_tree.

findings.evidence: The description is 978 of 1024 characters and opens with a declarative "Folds a finished GSD or superpowers plan's commits...". It spends most of its length on a list of internal mechanics (codebase-memory-mcp and graphify refresh, unit brief) instead of user intent.
findings.fix: Use when a finished GSD or superpowers plan's task commits should become one commit per logical feature (backup tag, tree check), when asked which plans are unfolded, or when ai-kit's unit flow must start, brief, checkpoint-push, ready, restack, hotfix or merge-chain a stacked phase branch, including before plan-phase or execute-phase of a GSD phase in a unit-flow repo and GSD hook install, even without the word fold. Not for squashing a branch, interactive rebases, a plain git push or gh pr create outside a recorded unit, a bare codebase-memory-mcp or graphify run, or an ordinary hotfix commit.

findings.evidence: "The engine is `scripts/fold.py` in this skill's folder. It has three forms:" This is not true: `fold.py --help` lists status, index, gsd-health and more. `status` appears only later, under Missed folds (line 200).
findings.fix: Say "The fold has three forms" and add a line that points to `python3 scripts/fold.py --help` for the full subcommand list (status, index, gsd-health). Alternatively, list `status --phase N` (read-only) next to the three fold forms.

findings.evidence: "When the `jev-fast-decision` skill is installed, the grouping choice can be proposed through its entry point." This gives no command and no default, so the agent has to guess how to call it, even though grouping is a fragile choice.
findings.fix: Say that the rule-based grouping is the default, and give the exact jev entry-point invocation (or say that fold.py calls it itself), so the agent never improvises the proposal.

findings.evidence: The 13 evals cover fold, install, consent, restack, merge-chain and refusals, but none exercises `fold.py start`, `boundary --point plan` or `ready`/`not_verified`. These are the GSD-hook steps the agent must run by hand. The trigger queries are 12 positive and 11 negative; no positive covers restack, hotfix or merge-chain wording.
findings.fix: Add an eval such as 'Phase 12 is verified as passed; mark its PR ready' with assertions that fold.py ready --phase 12 runs and that a not_verified refusal is reported, not worked around. Add one for 'before plan-phase 12' that asserts boundary-plan runs (start first when discuss was skipped). Add 2 positive trigger queries about restacking after a lower-unit commit and starting a hotfix unit.

findings.evidence: The `fold.py restack [...]` bullet is one 8-line sentence that mixes the local pass, remote-trunk rebases, catch-up push conditions, the cascade with push and abort semantics. It is hard to tell which case pushes and which does not.
findings.fix: Split it into a small decision list. (a) A lower unit moved: local restack, nothing pushed; the next checkpoint or start catch-up pushes, under consent, the units that were already pushed at their local tips. (b) No lower unit moved but the remote trunk moved: cascade and push under consent. (c) `--abort` restores every branch and the stack record. (d) `--continue` finishes a paused restack (see Cascade conflicts).

findings.evidence: The flow refusal table has no rows for refusals that SKILL.md itself names: `not_started`, `signal_order`, `not_verified`, `branch_missing`, `no_gates`, `bad_resolution`, `not_ready`/`ship_redirect`. For each one the agent has to search the text or load unit-contract.md.
findings.fix: Add one-line rows. not_started: check out the unit branch or run start. signal_order: run checkpoint --final first. not_verified: wait for the verifier to pass. branch_missing: show the owner. not_ready/ship_redirect: run ready, then send the owner to fold.py merge-chain. Alternatively, state that every unlisted reason is in references/unit-contract.md.
